question: How often do predefined feature relationships fail before and after each unchanged archived footprint?
dataset: The exact 119571 by 70 prepared matrix and label vector verified in the seed-0 run
tolerance_rule: Inequality violation: left > right + atol + rtol * max(abs(left), abs(right)). Equality uses absolute difference against the same tolerance. Strict sensitivity uses zero tolerances. Positive-rate sign rules have no tolerance.
tolerance_reason: Primary diagnostic allows small float32 rounding differences; exact comparisons are reported separately. These are audit tolerances, not reproduction acceptance thresholds.
strata: all records and each of the four classes
all, eligible and ineligible under the original bidirectional mask
rules: Directional and overall maxima do not exceed corresponding byte totals
Directional and overall packet-length means lie between minima and maxima
Directional mean agrees with directional bytes divided by packet count (extractor semantics diagnostic)
Positive byte/packet numerator and positive duration require a positive corresponding rate
evaluable: Finite compared values; positive relevant packet count for length rules; nonnegative length values for length bounds. Rate checks require finite positive duration and numerator. Evaluable counts are reported before and after.
transitions: introduced among rows evaluable before and after
resolved among rows evaluable before and after
after violations in rows previously unevaluable
before violations in rows now unevaluable
controls: Input CSV hashes and sizes match seed-0
Prepared X, y, feature order and shape match seed-0
Ineligible records and all columns outside the 23-column allowed-change set remain exactly unchanged
outputs: Per-rule counts by class and eligibility, with denominators
Compact row masks for independent recounting
First three examples per rule, variant and transition
Versions, source/data hashes, status, warnings and logs
scope_boundaries: No classifier fits or performance comparisons
Assumes corresponding packet-length fields use the same byte basis; a flag requires interpretation
Directional mean equality is a semantic diagnostic, not proof of an extractor defect
No claim of real TLS or PQC traffic validation
No duration-unit assumption, absolute-rate reconstruction, global-mean equality, standard-deviation reconstruction or subflow consistency proof
No confidence intervals or tests treating overlapping rows/splits as independent
authorship: New audit and notebook prepared with assistant assistance; original source preserved unchanged.
